newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude falls with NYMEX before holiday.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude falls with NYMEX before holiday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices dropped Thursday in line with decreases on the New York crude oil futures market, traders said.
Local trade, meanwhile, was dead ahead of Friday's U.S. Independence Day holiday, with most traders absent much of the trade day, traders said.
The discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the regional benchmark, remained unchanged at $2.16 under August West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude.

Outright prices for ANS crude oil fell following news that United Nations and Iraqi officials finalized terms of crude oil sales agreement. Those reports erased concerns about supply shortages, lowering prices in the futures market.
August WTI dropped 78 cents a barrel to $19.56 a barrel.
Line 63 barrels also declined with the NYMEX market.
Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- edged up after a major oil company raised posted prices early this week.
